checkedCards.question: querab

checkedCards.question: an Bord

checkedCards.question: der Kiel

checkedCards.question: das Ruder

checkedCards.question: die Pinne

checkedCards.question: das Steuerrad

checkedCards.question: die Wasserlinie

checkedCards.question: der Tiefgang

checkedCards.question: die Krängung
checkedCards.rationale: Feminine noun, spelling, heeling definition and verb krängen are correct.

checkedCards.question: die Bilge

checkedCards.question: das Deck

checkedCards.question: das Cockpit
checkedCards.rationale: PONS confirms das Cockpit; Duden confirms die Plicht as its nautical synonym.

checkedCards.question: der Niedergang
checkedCards.rationale: Correct masculine nautical sense and companionway translation; entrance plus steps are appropriately described.

checkedCards.question: die Luke
checkedCards.rationale: Correct feminine noun and closable opening; deck/cabin-top context is suitable.

checkedCards.question: die Backskiste
checkedCards.rationale: Cockpit-seat stowage is the intended Backskiste sense; often qualifier is appropriate.

checkedCards.question: die Reling / die Relingsstütze
checkedCards.rationale: Related two-term set works; rail wires and upright posts are clearly distinguished by definition and figure.

checkedCards.question: der Bugkorb
checkedCards.rationale: Bow rail/pulpit correct; highlighted rigid rail is at the pointed bow.

checkedCards.question: der Heckkorb
checkedCards.rationale: Stern rail/pushpit correct; highlighted rigid rail is at the flat transom.

checkedCards.question: die Klampe
checkedCards.rationale: Feminine and cleat correct; illustrated fitting is a horn cleat, matching the definition.

checkedCards.question: der Mast
checkedCards.rationale: PONS confirms masculine mast; upright spar is correctly highlighted.

checkedCards.question: der Baum
checkedCards.rationale: PONS confirms masculine boom; figure highlights the spar beneath the sail foot.

checkedCards.question: das Vorstag
checkedCards.rationale: Correct neuter, forward mast support and forestay translation; diagram highlights the bow-leading stay.

checkedCards.question: das Achterstag
checkedCards.rationale: Correct neuter and aft mast support; diagram highlights the stern-leading backstay.

checkedCards.question: die Wanten
checkedCards.rationale: Plural and feminine singular are valid; lateral-support meaning and selected shrouds match.

checkedCards.question: das Fall
checkedCards.rationale: Correct neuter article, Fallen plural and hoisting meaning. Rigging image highlights the halyard beside the mast; no incorrect control is highlighted.

checkedCards.question: die Schot
checkedCards.rationale: Correct feminine noun and sheet function. The highlighted mainsheet is a valid example of the general term.

checkedCards.question: die Großschot
checkedCards.rationale: Correct compound, gender and mainsheet translation. Usually through its boom appropriately permits boomless arrangements.

checkedCards.question: die Fockschot
checkedCards.rationale: Correct feminine compound and jib-sheet translation; the answer distinguishes it from the mainsheet.

checkedCards.question: die Dirk
checkedCards.rationale: Correct topping-lift meaning and endpoints. Highlighted line runs from masthead to boom end, distinct from the dimmed backstay.

checkedCards.question: der Baumniederholer
checkedCards.rationale: Correct boom-vang/kicker equivalence and restraining function. Diagram highlights the diagonal control below the boom.

checkedCards.question: der Unterliekstrecker
checkedCards.rationale: Correct masculine compound and outhaul function: clew movement changes foot tension, not luff tension.

checkedCards.question: die Winsch
checkedCards.rationale: Correct feminine Winsch spelling and English winch meaning. Description identifies its loaded-line and mechanical-advantage purpose.

checkedCards.question: die Winschkurbel
checkedCards.rationale: Correct feminine compound and removable winch-handle function; manufacturer instructions describe handle insertion and removal.

checkedCards.question: der Block
checkedCards.rationale: Correct masculine nautical Block and housed-pulley definition; line redirection and tackle are appropriate uses.

checkedCards.question: das Großsegel
checkedCards.rationale: Correct neuter compound and mainsail translation in this modern yacht course. Main-mast qualifier avoids confusing a mizzen.

checkedCards.question: die Fock
checkedCards.rationale: Correct feminine Fock and jib equivalence. Explicit modern-yacht qualifier handles traditional-rig exceptions; non-overlap distinction is supported by sailmaker terminology.

checkedCards.question: die Genua
checkedCards.rationale: Correct feminine Genua and English Genoa spelling. Mast overlap correctly distinguishes this sail from the preceding jib.

checkedCards.question: der Spinnaker
checkedCards.rationale: Correct masculine noun and English spelling. Broad reaching/downwind description is valid without claiming one precise wind-angle limit.

checkedCards.question: die Segellatte
checkedCards.rationale: Correct feminine compound and batten function. The sail-pocket and shape-support description covers both short and full-length battens.

checkedCards.question: das Vorliek / das Achterliek / das Unterliek
checkedCards.rationale: All three articles and edge translations are correct. Triangular-sail qualifier is useful; browser rendering highlights the correct luff, leech and foot.
checkedCards.finalQuestion: das Vorliek / das Achterliek / das Unterliek

checkedCards.question: der Segelkopf / der Hals / das Schothorn
checkedCards.rationale: All three articles and corner translations are correct. Browser rendering puts tack at the mast, clew aft, head at the top; three related terms are an acceptable recall set.
checkedCards.finalQuestion: der Segelkopf / der Hals / das Schothorn

checkedCards.question: Luv / Lee
checkedCards.rationale: Correct Luv/Lee directional pairing. Wind arrows and highlighted windward/leeward positions agree; dimmed shore labels do not reverse the boat-side meanings.

checkedCards.question: der wahre Wind
checkedCards.rationale: Correct adjective inflection and true-wind distinction. The text intentionally stays at introductory level and does not assert a disputed water-versus-ground reference.

checkedCards.question: der scheinbare Wind
checkedCards.rationale: Correct adjective inflection and apparent-wind meaning. Combining with the effect of motion avoids the mistaken scalar addition of wind speeds.

checkedCards.question: die Bö
checkedCards.rationale: Correct feminine article, Bö/Böe variants, Böen plural and gust meaning; the rare-looking short form is standard, not a typo.

checkedCards.question: am Wind / Halbwind / raumschots / vor dem Wind
checkedCards.rationale: Four tightly related points of sail are within the requested grouping scope. Instructor sources support this beginner close-hauled use of am Wind; beam, broad and dead-downwind descriptions are coherent.
checkedCards.finalQuestion: am Wind / Halbwind / raumschots / vor dem Wind

checkedCards.question: im Wind
checkedCards.rationale: Correct head-to-wind meaning. The statement concerns sail drive rather than claiming a boat cannot retain forward momentum or move under engine.

checkedCards.question: anluven
checkedCards.rationale: Correct infinitive and head-up/luff-up translation. Direction is relative to wind, not a fixed port/starboard turn.

checkedCards.question: abfallen
checkedCards.rationale: Correct infinitive and bear-away/bear-off translation. Opposite direction to anluven is stated unambiguously.

checkedCards.question: wenden
checkedCards.rationale: Correct bow-through-wind maneuver and established preparatory command. Ready about is a recognized English equivalent, distinct from the execution command.

checkedCards.question: halsen
checkedCards.rationale: Correct stern-through-wind maneuver, gybe/jibe variants and preparatory command. ISAF instruction uses Stand by to gybe.

checkedCards.question: kreuzen
checkedCards.rationale: Correct upwind beating meaning. Successive tacks describes the maneuver sequence without confusing kreuzen with a single turn.

checkedCards.question: die Segel setzen
checkedCards.rationale: Set/hoist matches setzen; raise or deploy accommodates conventional and furling sails. Großsegel setzen is a valid infinitive command.

checkedCards.question: die Segel bergen
checkedCards.rationale: Bergen correctly means taking sails out of use; phrasing does not wrongly restrict the term to downhauling. Correct verb and object.

checkedCards.question: reffen
checkedCards.rationale: Reffen means reducing set sail area. Infinitive and Großsegel example are correct.

checkedCards.question: dichtholen
checkedCards.rationale: Dichtholen means hauling in, with sheet in valid for the stated Schot example; no direction reversal.

checkedCards.question: fieren
checkedCards.rationale: Fieren correctly translates as controlled easing or paying out, opposite to dichtholen; Schot example is valid.

checkedCards.question: die Leine
checkedCards.rationale: Leine is feminine and line/rope is a suitable beginner translation; role-specific names are appropriately acknowledged.

checkedCards.question: der Palstek
checkedCards.rationale: Palstek is masculine and bowline is the fixed-loop knot. Explicit bowline/bow line distinction avoids confusion with a mooring line.

checkedCards.question: der Webeleinstek
checkedCards.rationale: Webeleinstek is an accepted spelling of the masculine clove hitch. Post/rail and fender-line usage are appropriate; card does not claim universal security.

checkedCards.question: der Achtknoten
checkedCards.rationale: Achtknoten is masculine; figure-of-eight is the stopper knot described, not the loop variant. Near the end does not instruct tying without a tail.

checkedCards.question: eine Leine aufschießen
checkedCards.rationale: Eine Leine aufschießen correctly disambiguates coiling from the sailing maneuver also called aufschießen; orderly loops for stowage is accurate.

checkedCards.question: der Festmacher
checkedCards.rationale: Festmacher is masculine and means a mooring line/warp in this boating context; berth or mooring use is appropriate.

checkedCards.question: die Vorleine / die Achterleine
checkedCards.rationale: Both line nouns are feminine. Bow line leads forward from bow; stern line leads aft from stern. Reused SVG highlights those exact leads with bow to the right.

checkedCards.question: die Vorspring / die Achterspring
checkedCards.rationale: Both springs are feminine. Vorspring runs aft from forward boat and checks forward motion; Achterspring runs forward from aft boat and checks aft motion. English-name variation is explicitly acknowledged. SVG lead geometry and restraint captions agree.

checkedCards.question: der Fender
checkedCards.rationale: Fender is masculine, translates directly, and cushioning description is correct. Figure points to the separate cushions on the boat side facing the pontoon; other labels are subdued.

checkedCards.question: anlegen
checkedCards.rationale: Anlegen in a sailing context correctly means berthing/coming alongside; other berth wording avoids restricting the verb to parallel mooring.

checkedCards.question: ablegen
checkedCards.rationale: Ablegen correctly means departure from berth. Cast off is an accepted English boating equivalent and departure definition prevents ambiguity with removing clothing.

checkedCards.question: festmachen
checkedCards.rationale: Festmachen correctly covers securing a boat or line. German infinitive command is natural and Make the line fast is correct seamanship English.

checkedCards.question: der Anker
checkedCards.rationale: Anker is masculine. Anchor and lowering it to the bottom to hold the boat are correct; no misleading anchoring procedure is asserted.

checkedCards.question: die Ankerkette
checkedCards.rationale: Ankerkette is feminine and anchor chain is correct. Chain connecting anchor to boat and possible chain/rope rode are accurate.

checkedCards.question: der Kompass
checkedCards.rationale: Kompass is masculine and correctly means compass. Direction relative to north does not falsely guarantee true north for every compass.

checkedCards.question: der Kurs
checkedCards.rationale: Kurs is masculine and correctly means course. Generic direction wording plus explicit distinction between steered and over-ground course avoids conflating them.

checkedCards.question: die Seemeile
checkedCards.rationale: Seemeile is feminine and nautical mile is correct. 1,852 metres is the exact unit in English thousands-separator notation.

checkedCards.question: der Knoten (Geschwindigkeit)
checkedCards.rationale: Knoten is masculine. One nautical mile per hour is correct; speed qualifier on front and rope-knot note disambiguate the homonym.

checkedCards.question: die Flaute
checkedCards.rationale: Flaute is feminine; calm with little or no wind is suitable vocabulary-level wording, consistent with very low Beaufort-zero winds.

checkedCards.question: die Rettungsweste
checkedCards.rationale: Rettungsweste is feminine and lifejacket is accurate. Flotation description and anlegen command are correct; no unsupported safety guarantee is made.

checkedCards.question: der Rettungsring
checkedCards.rationale: Rettungsring is masculine and correctly means lifebuoy/life ring. Throwing flotation to a person in the water matches DLRG usage.

checkedCards.question: der Lifebelt
checkedCards.rationale: Lifebelt is masculine and in German denotes the safety harness, distinct from its tether. SECUMAR explicitly calls it Lifebelt/Harness and confirms integrated examples.

checkedCards.question: Mann über Bord!
checkedCards.rationale: Mann über Bord and Mensch über Bord are established German alarm expressions. Both man/person overboard translations and meaning are accurate.

findings.claim: The card teaches the neuter article das for Freibord, but standard German uses der Freibord.
findings.scenario: A beginner memorises the question das Freibord and later produces that incorrect noun gender; the course promises noun articles and directly teaches this form.
findings.evidenceSummary: Duden lists masculine Freibord and gives der Freibord; Collins independently gives masculine inflection. The English meaning and reused drawing are correct.
findings.suggestedCorrection: Change the heading to der Freibord, keep the card ID, and rebuild web/courses/sailing-in-german/cards.json.

independentVerification.method: Read original anchored card and decision list before checking final candidate. Searched primary dictionaries for masculine/neuter alternatives; directly opened Duden. Parsed both source and deployment JSON, compared by stable card ID, and independently parsed final Markdown using the existing compiler without writing build outputs.

findings.concrete_failure: The German prompt teaches neuter das Freibord, while standard dictionary usage is masculine der Freibord. The learner can memorize an incorrect noun article.
findings.refutation_attempt: Checked whether a dictionary accepts neuter as an alternative or whether this is a different non-nautical sense. Duden specifies masculine for the nautical height above the waterline. A second dictionary also marks Freibord masculine. No applicable terminology ruling or supported neuter alternative was found.

evidence.supports: The entry heading is Freibord, der and the word class is Substantiv, maskulin. The definition concerns height above the waterline.
